title: The number of colours at a vertex is at most its degree
statement: Let $G$ be a finite loopless graph, and let $\mathscr{C}$ be a $k$-edge colouring of $G$, that is, an arbitrary assignment of one of the colours $1, 2, \ldots, k$ to each edge (not necessarily proper). For a vertex $v$, write $c(v)$ for the number of distinct colours represented at $v$, and $d(v)$ for its degree. Then \[c(v) \le d(v).\]
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite (loopless simple) graph
C is a k-edge colouring, i.e. a function from edges to Fin k
v is a vertex of G
replaced:
(6.3): \texttt{c(v) $\le$ d(v)}.

Clearly, we always have
\[c(v) \le d(v) \qquad (6.3)\]
